title: Emmanuel's exact 9 EMA / 20 SMA / 200 SMA day-trading rules on TSLA
market: TSLA, US stock, regular hours 09:30-16:00 ET, Nasdaq lit prints
data: /Volumes/Moon 26/tick_data/databento/xnas_basic_trades/TSLA/ (TSLA_2024-07.parquet ... TSLA_2026-06.parquet + TSLA_2026-06-25_2026-09-24.parquet), publisher_id 81 only, 2024-07-01 -> 2026-09-23, 557 days, 217,186 1m bars. Degraded days 2024-07-25, 2025-12-15, 2026-01-12 skipped. Daily 200 SMA usable from 2025-04-21.

headline.label: Exact rules, net of costs: in-sample / out-of-sample return
headline.value: +2.5% / +5.3% on 88/36 trades; t-stat 0.51 / 1.27 (not significant). Random entries same day + side beat it in 84% of runs IS, 13% OOS

stats.costs: 1 bp per side + $0.005 slippage per side on every fill (about 2.5-3 bp round trip at TSLA prices). Zero-cost numbers shown next to each.
stats.sizing: 1x notional per trade (no leverage), compounded. Video gives no size or risk per trade.

control_no_gap_bias.params: IS-best pullback, both sides every day

grid_note: IS stats in trades/win_rate/avg_R/profit_factor/return_pct, OOS stats in oos_*. Pullback rows shown with block=0.3% and exit R2 / trail only; the full 16,524-row grid is in grid_rows.pkl. Every swept number is one the video leaves out.

claims.claim: Never trade a flat / sideways 20 SMA (it is chop)
claims.test: All gap-direction touches of the 9 EMA on his time-of-day timeframes, 2R target, stop under trigger bar. Avg net R by 20 SMA slope (ATR per bar; 'flat' cut-off is a sweep, video leaves it out).
claims.result: flat (<0.03 ATR/bar) avg R -0.029 (n=313) vs sloped 0.03-0.25 avg R -0.080; steep>0.25 avg R +0.083

claims.claim: More prior touches of the 20 SMA that held = more reliable
claims.test: Same raw signals with a rising (falling) 20 SMA. Avg net R by how many touch episodes held earlier in the same 20 SMA run (touch = low within 0.1 ATR of the 20 and close holds it; video leaves the definition out).

claims.claim: Far from the 20 SMA = exit zone, not entry zone
claims.test: Every 5m bar in a trend (20 SMA sloped, price and 9 EMA on the trend side). Next 30 min return in the trend direction, bucketed by distance from the 20 SMA in ATRs (threshold is a sweep, video leaves it out).

claims.claim: After the trend accelerates, skip the FIRST pullback / breakout
claims.test: Filtered pullback signals (trend + alignment), 2R exit. Compare the first pullback after a bar more than 2.5 ATR from the 20 SMA (video leaves the number out) vs all other pullbacks.
claims.result: first pullback after acceleration avg R -0.105 (n=482), win 32.8%; other pullbacks avg R -0.042 (n=1148), win 35.6%
claims.verdict: WEAK (right direction, about 1 standard error, not proven)

claims.claim: Gap up = look long, gap down = look short (gap days trend)
claims.test: Per day: does the 09:30-16:00 move follow the gap? Plus: the IS-chosen setup traded BOTH ways every day, split by with-gap vs against-gap.
claims.result: close follows gap: <0.5% gap 46% of 147 days; 0.5-1% gap 49% of 128 days; 1-2% gap 59% of 163 days; 2-3% gap 64% of 66 days; >3% gap 50% of 48 days. Trades with gap avg R +0.193 (n=325) vs against gap +0.049 (n=200)
claims.verdict: SUPPORTED in 2024-25, FADED in 2026 OOS (gap-direction hold 10:00-16:00 on 1-3% gaps: +65 bp/day IS, +6 bp/day OOS)

claims.claim: The 200 SMA acts as support / resistance and is the target
claims.test: First touch of the 1h and daily 200 SMA each day (after 30 min on one side): does price stay rejected 60 min later? Placebo = same test on the 200 shifted 1% up and down. Plus: trades with a 200 SMA within 0.3% in the way vs not.
claims.result: 1h 200: rejected 41.8% (n=55) vs placebo 38.7% (n=124); daily 200 (from 2025-04-21): rejected 60.9% (n=23) vs placebo 58.6% (n=58). Exact-system trades with a 200 target hit it 3.8% of the time (n=52). Trades with a 200 within 0.3% in the way avg R -0.080 (n=61) vs clear -0.060
claims.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED (real 200 rejects about as often as a fake level 1% away; target almost never hit)

claims.claim: Two moving averages are all you need (the MAs are the edge)
claims.test: Random-entry control: same days, same side, same hold time as the real trades, random start minute, same costs. 1000 runs.
claims.result: Exact rules: random beats real 84% of runs IS, 13% OOS. IS-picked base breakout: random beats real 87% IS, 99% OOS.
claims.verdict: NOT PROVEN: exact rules lost to random IS and beat it OOS on only 36 trades; the IS-best version lost to random 99% of runs OOS

price_replay.note: best OOS day of the IS-chosen version (picked as the best day, so it flatters the system)

takeaways: Exact rules (gap 1%+, rising 20 SMA under price, 9 over 20, both timeframes agree, doji / tail trigger, 2 prior touches, skip first pullback after a 2.5 ATR stretch, no 200 SMA within 0.3%, trail under pivots): 88 IS trades +2.5%, 36 OOS trades +5.3% net. Small, not significant.
Stack EVERY literal rule (also the 'pullback to the 20 on the fast chart = 9 EMA on the slow chart' touch) and TSLA gives 4 trades in 2.2 years. The rules are a filter so tight it barely trades.

The MA filters DO beat the raw pullback entry (raw: -0.6% IS, -10.7% OOS net). But random entries on the same days and side BEAT the exact rules IS (8.7 bp random vs 2.9 bp real per trade) and lost to them OOS (6.0 vs 14.6 bp, only 36 trades).

Best IS version (best_base, picked from 16,524 combos by IS t-stat): +129% IS, then +11.5% OOS (PF 1.261). Random entries same day + side beat it 99% of runs OOS. The IS money came from the gap direction, not the MAs.

Gap bias was the real piece in 2024-25: 1-2% gaps kept going 59% of days, 2-3% gaps 64%. Just holding the gap direction from 10:00 to 16:00 on 1-3% gap days made +65 bp a day IS but only +6 bp a day OOS. It faded in 2026.

Extension is NOT an exit signal on TSLA: in a trend, the next 30 min return gets BIGGER the further price is from the 20 SMA (in zone -0.3 bp, over 3.5 ATR +4.8 bp). Flat vs sloped 20 SMA, touch count and the 200 SMA as support / resistance all showed no real edge vs placebo.
Costs matter: raw pullback entries make +47% IS at zero cost and -0.6% after 1 bp + half a cent per side. Tight 1m / 2m stops make the cost a big slice of 1R.
equity_curve_note: equity_curve = exact rules, net, 1x notional compounded. equity_curve_chosen = IS-chosen best_base
